messages:
Ivy (PM): Starting a thread for a packaging proposal: 'Route Priority Credits' (RPC). Concept: customers buy credits to attach short-lived priority windows to specific API routes to reduce tail latency during bursts. Need input on pricing shapes, launch criteria, and contract guardrails.

Rahul (Eng): Implementation sketch: credits are checked at ingress, cheap lookup, then requests get a priority bit for N seconds. Two enforcement modes: soft-priority (weighted scheduler) vs hard-reserve (dedicated slots). Hard-reserve requires capacity reservations.

Dana (DevEx): Console requirements: route-level config, credit balance, schedule windows, and event timeline indicating when credits were consumed. Also a preview of expected delta in latency under typical spikes. Minimal pilot UI is enough.

Chris (Sales): Distinguish RPC from account-wide priority. Customers ask for route granularity. Sales packaging: monthly bundles and emergency top-ups. Pilot offer: 200 credits free for early pilot + discounted top-ups.

Lena (Legal): Important: do not market RPC as an SLA. If we offer hard-reserve variant, that must carry explicit SLA and pricing. Recommend default language: "best-effort priority; not a guaranteed latency SLA unless reserved." Add burn cap and misuse clause.

Omar (Finance): Quick margin thinking: need cost-per-credit model. If soft-priority rarely causes additional infra, pricing can be premium markup. For hard-reserve, model like reserved capacity seat with monthly commitment. We must flag revenue recognition rules for bundled credits.

Ivy (PM): Proposed pilot scope: implement soft-priority RPC, pilot with 3 customers, expose route toggle + one-click auto-apply for deploys, telemetry, and simple billing entries. Launch criteria: measurable reduction in 95th/99th latencies for target routes, platform cost increase <7% at 99th percentile, and two pilot customers reporting positive signal.

Rahul (Eng): Rough estimate: spec ~3-5 days, infra + routing changes 2 sprints, console hooks 1 sprint. Need a canary plan and an emergency kill-switch to disable RPC globally. Also add a fallback policy: if credit balance exhausted, revert immediately to normal routing.

Dana (DevEx): UX edge-cases: show per-route historical credit usage, explain how credits map to time windows, and allow scheduled windows (e.g., deploys or known traffic events). Also need to surface billing attribution.

Chris (Sales): Suggested SKUs: RPC-200 ($79/mo, 200 credits), RPC-1000 ($299/mo, 1000 credits), PAYG $0.40/credit. We can tweak after pilot. Also capture use-cases: deploy-time smoothing, marketing campaign spikes, seasonal events.

Lena (Legal): Pilot T&Cs: no guaranteed latency, automatic rollback clause if customer uses RPC to bypass contractual usage limits, and audit logging requirement. For enterprise pilots, include an explicit opt-in for traffic steering and a rollback SLA.

Omar (Finance): Add note: accounting should treat prepaid bundles as deferred revenue; include provisioning to adjust churn assumptions if customers buy top-ups frequently.

Ivy (PM): Ops request: run a sim comparing baseline vs RPC soft-priority under a 5-minute 8x spike for a route that normally gets 20% of traffic. Looking for credit burn, effect on tail latency, and impact on CPU/GPU. @sim-bot can you run?

sim-bot: Simulation queued: "RPC soft-priority 8x spike 5min" job #8812. ETA ~2h. Will post summary here when done.

Rahul (Eng): Security note: audit events must include which route consumed credits and the caller ID. If RPC allows steering to different model pools, we need to respect IAM and KMS boundaries.

Dana (DevEx): I'll mock Console flows and example API for attaching credits to a route. Will include example CLI snippet for infra teams.

Ivy (PM): Next actions: Rahul -> tech spec + kill-switch design; Dana -> Console mocks + API example; Lena -> pilot T&Cs draft; Chris -> shortlist 3 pilot customers; Omar -> refine preliminary pricing model. I'll assemble PRD by EOD next Friday. Thanks :rocket:
